lead: Sunday was a model-release day with an edge: [Qwen Image 2.1](../summaries/1ba4b92c727b.md) and [Grok 4.7](../summaries/e17843d4d54b.md) shared the front page with [Google's AX, an open agentic orchestrator](../summaries/07975f32cf7b.md) and a much-loved [visual explainer of transformers](../summaries/0e47888f345c.md). The week's money doubts surfaced early - [Wall Street grew skeptical of the data-center boom](../summaries/6564dd7e87a6.md) - and [Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent from shopping on amazon.com](../summaries/41d477801352.md).

sections.title: Release Sunday: Qwen, Grok and Google's orchestrator
sections.intro: Image generation, a new Grok, and Google open-sourcing an agentic orchestrator - twice told.

sections.title: The case against careless AI coding
sections.intro: CI reworked for agent throughput, a quality-management rebuttal, another 'don't write with AI' essay, and a Kool-Aid deconversion.

sections.title: Agents meet the marketplace
sections.intro: Amazon slamming the door on Meta's shopping agent, intent conflicts between parallel coding agents, and a personal memory that never summarizes.

sections.title: Money and meritocracy doubts
sections.intro: Skepticism about the data-center boom, AI and the end of upward mobility, college coming apart, and a 'drop dead' message to humanity.

sections.title: The risk debate, in every register
sections.intro: Doctorow's Claude Delusion, Andrew Ng calling extinction fears science fiction, an antitrust suit over slowdown coordination, Altman at the UN, and chatbots failing financial queries.

sections.title: Weekend hardware and oddities
sections.intro: An M5 Ultra Mac Studio review, frontier AI on your own hardware, escaping macOS 27's model downloads and Siri, and continual learning on 8GB of VRAM.
